A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe ND-SDF and include the main paper and appendices A–D. Text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on four datasets, quantitative component ablations, and qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original reconstruction experiments and ablations, revises some numerical results, and adds diagnostic visualizations.

M1.justification: The quaternion deflection network, adaptive prior losses, angle-guided optimization, partial unbiased rendering, and warm-up procedure are retained. The explicit angle-map update and curvature-loss schedule add implementation detail without establishing a changed underlying algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate indoor reconstruction on ScanNet, Replica, Tanks and Temples, and ScanNet++, including the existing alternative-prior and mesh-resolution comparisons. The new diagnostics examine retained reconstruction conditions rather than adding a dataset, domain, or distinct task.

E2.justification: ScanNet Table 1 adds DebSDF and H2OSDF and removes Unisurf. Unisurf remains in the Replica comparison, and comparator membership in the other benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: New diagnostics compare rendering profiles with and without unbiasing and three pixelwise normal losses; Appendix A.3.3 also reports a curvature-loss omission control. Existing benchmark metrics, scene counts, image resolution, and 128,000-step training budget remain unchanged. Table 8's newly explicit ScanNet label does not establish a dataset switch because v1 leaves its dataset unclear.

E4.justification: New Figure 3 examines erroneous density and rendering weights near a chair leg, and Figure 9 compares naive, deflected, and adaptive normal-loss heatmaps. Appendix A.3.3 adds a qualitative finding that removing curvature regularization has little effect. Existing component, prior-model, warm-up, and depth-loss ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The method's bias-confidence function is not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises ND-SDF's ScanNet results, including F-score 78.6 to 82.0 and precision 84.9 to 84.0, alongside changed comparator rows. Table 8 replaces 0.662/0.686 with 0.707/0.746; its unclear earlier setting prevents interpreting this as a same-setting gain. Tables 2–7 and 9–10 retain their numbers, while the new diagnostics add qualitative findings.

T1.justification: New Eq. 22 formally defines the maintained angle map through a maximum-and-decay recurrence, whereas v1 only describes dynamic maintenance. The existing loss mathematics and view-dependent-density argument are retained; the density prefactor is also made explicit as 1/beta instead of alpha. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: adaptive normal-prior use, recovery of detailed and smooth geometry, and superior indoor reconstruction. Additional comparisons and stronger wording do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 attributes curvature regularization's small benefit to monocular cues already constraining smooth regions. It also interprets the new loss heatmaps and explains why stored angle maps are needed before volume compositing. The limitations concerning dependence on priors, sparse coverage, and local optima remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 specifies angle-map initialization and updating, explains stored-map use, and discloses exponential decay of curvature regularization. Reported training time changes from about 12 hours to 14 GPU hours. Captions identify ablation datasets and explicitly associate Tanks and Temples Table 2 with resolution 768; code-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list and substantive positioning against prior filtering, uncertainty weighting, and probabilistic approaches are unchanged. The expanded introduction discusses VolSDF and NeuS, which were already covered in related work; the newly compared baselines were already cited.

P1.justification: Sentence-level editing throughout corrects terminology and grammar, refines method and experiment descriptions, and expands selected explanations. Examples include correcting 'Normal Ddeflection' and 'Normal Deviation' and renaming Appendix A.3. The section hierarchy and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 3 and 9, redraws the modulation plot to show both weighting functions, and adds enlarged details to the component-ablation visualization. Tables 7–9 are transposed, and several displays move or receive expanded captions. Most existing reconstruction images are retained.

improvement.justification: The added ScanNet comparators, diagnostic figures, and explicit implementation details make the evidence and procedure easier to assess. These are useful, limited gains rather than a substantially different validation of the work. The reasons for the revised Table 1 and Table 8 scores remain unexplained, limiting what can be concluded from those numerical changes.
